title: AI papers — arXiv announcement batch 11 Nov 2026: 8 selected papers
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering, and citation evidence is limited for papers announced within the last day.

sections.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
sections.abstract: ReTrace turns an SOP and logged agent runs into executable workflows where code selects each next step, reporting modest completion trade-offs alongside lower cost and much shorter latency on its tested procedures.
sections.ranking_evidence: Multiple independent technical commentaries discuss the latency/cost trade-off and where compilation is unsafe; the paper reports 79 production procedures and two public benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors extract rules from agent reasoning and tool-call traces, then compile the rules into planner-free executable workflows; on tau-squared-Bench they report 1.3 seconds per task versus 170 seconds for the agent.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say construction checks do not establish that recovered conditions are correct; results test new inputs to the same procedures, not transfer to new procedures, and changes to SOPs/tools may require rebuilding.

sections.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
sections.abstract: The paper replaces single-hypothesis testing with contrast sets of competing explanations, reporting that the framing resolves more questions from the same evidence and experiment budget across six datasets.
sections.ranking_evidence: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, cross-listed in three core AI categories, and discussed in independent technical coverage; the paper reports six-domain results and a blinded expert study.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 67% more resolved questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget and expert agreement on 78% of resolved questions.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors limit experiments to tabular observational datasets and one GPT-4o-backed agent; conclusions are statistical rather than causal, and generated contrast sets can omit plausible alternatives.

sections.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
sections.abstract: The authors report that Bonbon, trained on paired protein–ligand sequences, supports zero-shot interaction predictions and prospective compound screening, with a sharp capability increase at the largest of six tested scales.
sections.ranking_evidence: Listed as a NeurIPS 2026 main-track oral and covered independently by Astrobiology; the paper reports prospective wet-lab validation across nine targets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim one frozen sequence-trained representation supports functional, residue-level, and bond-level interaction predictions, reporting a 61.5% dose-response hit rate for de novo compounds in prospective tests.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the reported capabilities are coarse-grained; explicit 3D-coordinate extraction and properties such as residence time and dissociation kinetics were not studied, and results use frozen representations.

sections.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
sections.abstract: WikiTrace links each agent-memory lesson to its source summary and trajectory, letting an agent revisit evidence when a lesson is ambiguous, conflicting, or drawn from a failed task; the authors report gains across five agentic benchmarks.
sections.ranking_evidence: Discussed by independent technical coverage, with a public implementation and project page; it reports results across five benchmarks and eight suites.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report top performance on all evaluated suites, a 3.2-point average improvement over an insights-only baseline, and lower memory-induced regression when source evidence is available.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that source links let agents check but do not verify an insight; including all insights in the initial prompt makes memory grow, and scalable retrieval is left open.

sections.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
sections.abstract: FGSE temporarily tests proposed memory updates as structured hypotheses on transfer, falsification, and regression probes before committing, refining, or rejecting them; the authors report results across web, app, tool-use, and long-term-memory benchmarks.
sections.ranking_evidence: Listed as a NeurIPS 2026 poster, cross-listed in AI and machine learning, and reports multi-environment safety and task-performance evaluations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report reduced falsification failures, regression damage, and harmful committed updates while retaining benchmark performance, supporting verifier-gated rather than immediate memory writes.
sections.unique_caveat: The approach is framed for verifier-rich environments; extending it to settings where verifiers must be learned or approximated, and to multimodal agents, remains future work.

sections.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
sections.abstract: AutoScaffold uses a frozen teacher to diagnose student-model training experience and adapt task-class strategies and hard-example hints, reporting improved scaffold-free results over corresponding RL baselines in four domains.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in machine learning and language, spans four task settings, and has multiple independent technical write-ups; its scaffold-removal evaluation makes the transfer claim checkable.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains over corresponding RL baselines on ALFWorld, search-based QA, math, and GPU-kernel generation after removing scaffolds at evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify reducing the cost of teacher interventions as future work; the reported gains are against corresponding baselines in the four evaluated domains, not all methods or settings.

sections.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
sections.abstract: Pyrite introduces a 1,500-pair protein–ligand pose-ranking benchmark and LLM agents that combine structured molecular representations, tool outputs, and learned features, reporting up to 74% accuracy.
sections.ranking_evidence: Presented in the NeurIPS 2026 Agentic AI for Biological Discovery Workshop, with a NeurIPS listing, OpenReview record, and public benchmark/code.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 74% pose-pair accuracy from LLM-guided feature discovery, exceeding observed expert performance, and report improvements from GRPO for open-weight models.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say an accuracy gap remains; training is limited to pre-AF3 structures, while transfer to other pose generators and full drug-discovery ranking pipelines remains untested.

sections.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
sections.abstract: Continual-ARC makes ARC tasks recur with fresh instances in a budgeted stream, comparing memory-based agent harnesses and weight-updating learners on memorization and generalization.
sections.ranking_evidence: A new benchmark protocol with released code and run records received independent technical discussion in multiple write-ups; it directly compares persistent harnesses and weight-based learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that harness persistence usually does not improve memorization without expert guidance, that tested harnesses did not improve unseen-task performance, and that weight-based learning did.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note most runs use relatively small models on the easiest ARC-AGI-1 track; stronger models and ARC-AGI-2/3 remain future work.
